# Milestone 9 — Docker

Completed and container-verified on 2026-09-24.

## Run locally

Requires Docker Engine with Docker Compose v2 (or Docker Desktop). No host Go or PostgreSQL installation is required for the container path. From the repository root:

```sh
cp .env.example .env
# Set JWT_SECRET in .env to a fresh value generated by: openssl rand -hex 32
docker compose up --build -d --wait
curl --fail http://localhost:8080/health
curl --fail http://localhost:8080/ready
```

Compose reads JWT_SECRET from the shell or .env; no JWT secret is built into the image. Empty/short secrets cause the API to exit with a sanitized configuration error. `.env.example` is also usable for host Go development; its localhost database URLs are deliberately not injected into containers. Compose explicitly uses the postgres service hostname. Set API_PORT or POSTGRES_PORT if the default host ports conflict. Both published ports bind to loopback only.

Fresh startup leaves users empty. To create the three explicitly local demo users:

```sh
make docker-seed
```

See [M3](milestone-3.md) for local demo credentials. Alternatively bootstrap a real initial local admin with environment variables you supply:

```sh
docker compose run --rm --no-deps \
  -e BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_NAME -e BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL -e BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD \
  --entrypoint /app/gowork-bootstrap api
```

Export those three variables before invoking the command, then unset them. Do not put credentials on command lines or commit them. Neither bootstrap nor demo seed runs during normal startup. Repeated explicit demo seeding does not overwrite accounts.

`make docker-up` builds/starts/waits; `make docker-down` stops/removes containers while preserving the database volume. `docker compose down --volumes` destroys that project's database and is only for an intentional local reset. Existing M2 database volumes and host-development commands remain supported.

## Container contract

- Builder is version-pinned `golang:1.27.1-bookworm`; modules are checked against go.sum. Runtime is scratch with static API, migration, bootstrap, seed and probe binaries plus migrations and CA roots. UID/GID 65532, direct API entrypoint, no shell or toolchain. Tags are version-pinned, not immutable digests; production release image digest recording remains M12.
- Build context uses an allowlist. No environment files, credentials, local binaries, Git history or tests enter the final image; build has no secret arguments. CA roots support the application's existing certificate-verifying production PostgreSQL TLS configuration.
- Compose dependency chain is postgres healthy → migration exits zero → grants exits zero → API. The migration runner alone receives MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL; grants alone receives the local owner password as PGPASSWORD. API receives only the restricted runtime DATABASE_URL and its signing configuration. Owner access is not granted to the API.
- Grants reuse `db/local/grants.sql`. A separate postgres-client one-shot service applies them after schema creation; this keeps SQL administration out of the API startup path and works on existing local volumes. Failure in either one-shot blocks API startup. Ordinary up may rerun these idempotent setup commands; it never runs down migrations or resets data. After source/schema changes, use `docker compose down` followed by `docker compose up --build -d --wait` to recreate the complete chain.
- API and migration root filesystems are read-only, drop all Linux capabilities, and disable privilege escalation. Compose is explicitly development-only, with public local database credentials and local plaintext database transport. Production must supply its own credentials, TLS, migration orchestration and restart policy.
- The image healthcheck probes /health (liveness). Local Compose overrides it to /ready so `up --wait` proves DB/schema readiness. Neither check itself restarts the process. The probe uses bounded loopback HTTP without proxies or redirects. PORT remains configurable in the image; Compose fixes the internal port to 8080 and permits changing the host API_PORT.
- Docker sends SIGTERM directly to the Go API. Compose grants 25 seconds, exceeding the application's 20-second drain deadline. PostgreSQL data uses the existing named volume.

## Verification

`make docker-smoke` requires Docker and Python 3. It creates a unique disposable `gowork-m9-*` Compose project, builds the image, and checks fresh startup, runtime user/read-only filesystem, credential separation, final image contents/CA roots, empty initial users, explicit seed, HTTP login/asset creation, repeated seed, down/up data and audit persistence, DB-outage liveness/readiness, graceful stop exit code, and migration-failure startup gating. Its cleanup removes only that generated project's containers and volume. Use unoccupied API_PORT/POSTGRES_PORT when running alongside another local stack.

The Docker packaging workflow runs the smoke check and `make check`; the existing database workflow retains all PostgreSQL regression tests and sqlc reproducibility. This is M9 packaging evidence; the broader M10 CI hardening and intentional test-failure gate demonstration remain planned.

Evidence: local `make check` passed on Go 1.27.1. [Docker packaging run 36025992396](https://github.com/Gyebran/GoWork/actions/runs/36025992396) passed all packaging checks on `75ed835e5b5d4950f8f200be7c984ac373d41d86`; measured final image size was 51,186,167 bytes (about 48.8 MiB, uncompressed, runner architecture). [PostgreSQL run 36025992402](https://github.com/Gyebran/GoWork/actions/runs/36025992402) passed the complete regression suite and reproducible sqlc on the same commit. The first Docker attempt exposed that script compatibility issue after passing startup/persistence/outage checks; the corrected full run above passed. Docker was not available in the editing workspace, so container verification ran on GitHub Actions. The completion commit changes documentation only. No deployment was performed.

References: [Docker multi-stage builds](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-concepts/building-images/multi-stage-builds/) and [Compose dependency order](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/startup-order/).
